original_text: 3.1.2.9 Operational Status and Control – The BE shall provide operational status data to and receive control data from the M&C System.

attribute_scores.rationale: The terminology is generally clear, though 'status data' and 'control data' lack explicit payload definitions.
Missing specific details regarding protocol, frequency of status updates, or error handling when communication fails.
Uses standard terms consistent with the backend architecture and M&C system naming conventions.
Uses the mandatory modal 'shall' and follows the standard actor-action structure.
Technically sound and standard practice for hardware/software integration in astronomy backends.
Combines two distinct operations into a single statement: providing status data AND receiving control data.
Testable via interface verification, but vagueness in data specifications makes test case derivation slightly difficult.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: provide operational status data to and receive control data from
shortcomings.explanation: The requirement mandates two distinct capabilities (transmitting status and receiving control) which should be separated into individual requirements to facilitate independent verification and traceability.
The requirement lacks specification of the types, formats, update rates, or specific parameters of the status and control data.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: This requirement establishes the interface and communication link between the Backend (BE) system and the Monitor and Control (M&C) System in a radio astronomy correlator backend, ensuring operational status telemetry is transmitted and control commands are received.

evaluations.original_problematic_excerpt: provide operational status data to and receive control data from
evaluations.context_reasoning: The combination of providing status and receiving control represents a single logical interface relationship between the Backend (BE) and the Monitor and Control (M&C) System (i.e., bidirectional M&C connectivity). Splitting them into separate requirements creates unnecessary fragmentation for what is fundamentally a unified architectural connection point specified by high-level standards.

At the architectural requirements level for complex radio astronomy backend systems, specifying exact data types, formats, and update rates inline is impractical and typically handled by external Interface Control Documents (ICDs) or lower-level software data models. The requirement correctly establishes the mandate for the interface without overburdening the high-level functional requirement with low-level implementation details.

layer2.reasoning_summary: Both candidate defects (DEF-1 regarding singularity and DEF-2 regarding completeness of data parameters) are pedantic false positives in the context of high-level interface requirements in large astronomical backend systems. High-level interface allocations frequently group status and control together as a single architectural responsibility toward a Monitor and Control (M&C) system, while specific telemetry items, formats, and update rates are deferred to interface control documents (ICDs) or lower-level data dictionary specifications rather than being embedded in top-level behavioral requirements.
